FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` returns remediation-outcome diagnoses and self-diagnosis diagnoses, but only `new_diagnoses` from the pre-verification checks are persisted into `self._diagnoses` via `self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)` before those later diagnoses are appended to the return list. As a result, `all_diagnoses`, `has_critical`, and `false_positive_rate`/history-based self-assessment operate on an incomplete state that excludes remediation outcomes and self-diagnosis outputs. This is a real correctness bug inside the immune layer’s own memory, not just logging, because later calibration logic consumes `self._diagnoses`.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `record_round()`, accumulate all emitted diagnoses first, then extend `self._diagnoses` once with the full set. For example: build `emitted = new_diagnoses + verification_results + self_diags`, persist `self._diagnoses.extend(emitted)`, then return `emitted`. Alternatively, append `verification_results` and `self_diags` to `_diagnoses` explicitly.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.false_positive_rate` claims to be a recent-window metric (“last 10 rounds”), but its denominator counts essentially all historical diagnoses in `self._diagnoses` with no round filter, while the numerator filters only `_false_positive_history` by recent rounds. Over time this forces the rate downward regardless of current false-positive behavior, so `self_diagnose()` can stop reacting to a genuinely bad recent false-positive regime. This breaks the Level-3 self-calibration loop.
PROPOSED_FIX: Store round indices for all diagnoses in a uniform way and compute both numerator and denominator over the same recent-round window. For example, persist diagnoses with `round` metadata and count only diagnoses within `[start_round, current_round]`, excluding informational detector types as intended.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` for a `FORMAT` failure instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. The method correctly returns `FailureType.FORMAT`, but the event stream misclassifies the boundary event. Any downstream consumer relying on event type to distinguish parse failures from format-compliance failures receives the wrong signal, undermining immune/monitoring separation.
PROPOSED_FIX: In the `if not response.format_compliant:` branch, emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` instead of `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.87
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` feeds incorrect failure status into `health_monitor.record_model_round()`. It sets `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`, which ignores timeout, empty, format, and underperform failures already detected by `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`. Therefore consecutive model-failure detection in the immune layer misses most actual failures and tracks a narrower condition than the rest of the system considers failure.
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive `failed` from the `failures` map produced earlier in `process_round()`, e.g. `failed = failures.get(mid) is not None`, and handle models absent from `responses` as failures too. If the monitor intentionally wants only transport/protocol failures, pass a richer failure category instead of a lossy boolean.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` calls `health_monitor.record_model_round(mid, fc, failed)` without `response_time` or `response_chars`, even though `record_model_round()` uses those fields for parser-yield anomaly detection and cost-per-finding spike detection. Because the defaults are `0.0` and `0`, both checks are effectively dead in integration despite being implemented in the monitor.
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass actual values when available: `response_time=responses[mid].response_time` and `response_chars=len(responses[mid].content)` for present responses; use explicit sentinel behavior for missing responses.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.89
DESCRIPTION: `apply_diagnosis()` records remediation state using the post-transform current value of the target metric, not the pre-transform baseline the verifier should compare against. The code snapshots `current_metric_val` before P-pass, then applies the transform, then recomputes `current_metric = self._get_current_metric(...)` and stores that into `set_remediation_state(metric_at_apply=...)`. Since the transform changes config, not the observed metric histories, this often equals the pre-value now — but architecturally it is wrong and brittle. More importantly, for deferred approvals it stores the metric at approval time while `applied_round` remains the original diagnosis round, misaligning baseline and elapsed-round verification.
PROPOSED_FIX: Capture and store the verification baseline immediately before applying or approving the remediation, and pair it with the actual application round. In `approve_deferred_remediation()`, use the approval-time round, not the original queued round, when calling `set_remediation_state`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83
DESCRIPTION: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` uses generic metric drift as its success criterion rather than checking whether the diagnosed pathology stopped. For `kappa_stuck`, any rise in `kappa` counts as success even if kappa is still effectively unusable; for `vocab_saturation`, a higher observed `vocab_growth` is treated as success even though the remediation changed the threshold, not the raw growth process; for `mu`, the tolerance allows deterioration up to 20% in absolute magnitude to still count as “improved.” This can clear ineffective remediations and poison step-effectiveness learning.
PROPOSED_FIX: Verify pathology-specific predicates instead of raw monotone drift. Examples: `kappa_stuck` succeeds only if recent kappa no longer satisfies the stuck predicate; `vocab_saturation` succeeds only if the detector would no longer fire under the new threshold; `findings_decline` succeeds only if the decline pattern breaks; `model_failure` succeeds only if the specific model’s consecutive-failure streak resets.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.91
DESCRIPTION: The immune remediation loop has an unguarded circularity: `apply_diagnosis()` mutates shared config such as `self.config.tau_sim`, which directly changes `ConvergenceDetector` behavior and also changes duplicate detection elsewhere via `_finding_similarity` threshold use. The immune monitor then judges the success of that remediation using downstream metrics generated by the mutated detector stack, without isolating detector recalibration from the measurement channel. This can create self-justifying success signals and oscillatory behavior rather than independent verification.
PROPOSED_FIX: Separate parameter-adjustment effects from outcome measurement. At minimum, log which detector configuration produced each post-fix metric and verify against pathology predicates over multiple rounds. Better: stage config changes with shadow evaluation or compare pre/post diagnosis predicates under fixed historical data before accepting success.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: Deferred remediation approval uses stale round information. `approve_deferred_remediation()` calls `_apply_transform()` now, but then records remediation state with `applied_round=deferred["round"]` — the original diagnosis round, not the approval/application round. If approval occurs later, `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` will think the remediation has already had multiple rounds to work and may verify/escalate it immediately against data from before the fix was ever applied.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a current-round parameter to `approve_deferred_remediation()` or derive it from live manager state, and use that as `applied_round`. Also store both `diagnosed_round` and `approved_round` separately in the deferred record.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive sensitivity mechanism is effectively broken. In `record_round()`, `effective_window()` reads `resolved` and `persistent`, but ignores `_sensitivity_decay` entirely and only widens the window additively via `resolved * _sensitivity_growth`. This contradicts the documented formula and makes self-adjustment of `sensitivity_decay` largely inert with respect to actual runtime detection sensitivity.
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement the documented adaptive rule consistently, e.g. combine multiplicative decay for resolved pathologies with controlled adjustment for persistence, and ensure `self_diagnose()` changes actually affect `effective_window()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F011
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: The `mu` pathology branch in `record_round()` emits diagnoses but never increments `self._pathology_counts["mu"]`. The resolution branch later checks `_pathology_counts.get("mu", 0) > 0`, so `mu` never develops persistence state and never records natural resolution through that path. This breaks adaptive sensitivity and resolution accounting specifically for one of the monitor’s core pathologies.
PROPOSED_FIX: When `mu_increasing and findings_not_increasing` is true, increment `self._pathology_counts["mu"]` similarly to the kappa and findings-decline branches, and include the occurrence count in evidence.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F012
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80
DESCRIPTION: Pathology keying is inconsistent across detection, resolution, and remediation for `mu`. Natural resolution checks use `"mu"` in `_pathology_counts` and `record_natural_resolution("mu")`, but the no-active-remediation guard checks `"mu_distortion" not in self._remediation_state`. Since the remediation chains do not key a `mu` pathology at all, this guard is mismatched and the state model is internally incoherent.
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalize pathology keys end-to-end. Use one canonical key per pathology for `_pathology_counts`, `_remediation_state`, `record_natural_resolution()`, and any future remediation chain entries.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F013
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` hardcodes vocab-saturation thresholds and window (`0.04`, `3`) because it is instantiated without access to the shared config, while `DynamicManagementConfig` exposes `tau_vocab_growth` and `vocab_sustained_window` and the diminishing-returns detector may be using different values. This creates split-brain behavior: the monitor diagnoses premature vocab saturation using different criteria than the main stop logic.
PROPOSED_FIX: Inject `DynamicManagementConfig` into `DetectorHealthMonitor` at construction and use `config.tau_vocab_growth` and `config.vocab_sustained_window` in Check 5.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F014
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: The immune layer emits several diagnoses with no remediation path: `parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, `cpf_spike`, `mu`, many `self_diagnosis` outputs, and parts of dispatch/verification handling. Since `apply_diagnosis()` silently returns `None` for these, large parts of the “self-healing” layer are observational only. Given the code’s own claims of autonomous remediation, this is a completeness gap in the immune response layer.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either add remediation chains for emitted diagnoses or explicitly classify such diagnoses as advisory-only in code and docs, with distinct detector types/severities so they are not mistaken for actionable autonomous findings.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F015
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: `record_round()` never resets `_pathology_counts["vocab_saturation"]` when the condition clears. Kappa and findings-decline have explicit resolution branches; vocab saturation does not. This leaves stale persistence state, inflates future occurrence counts, and prevents natural-resolution accounting for that pathology.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an `else` resolution branch for Check 5 that increments `_resolved_counts["vocab_saturation"]`, records natural resolution when no remediation is active, and resets `_pathology_counts["vocab_saturation"] = 0`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F016
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: Regression detection in `process_round()` can repeatedly warn on the same snapshot across rounds until cleanup, but it does not actually suppress future autonomous fixes despite claiming “Deferring further autonomous fixes for human review.” The code only emits an event and then trims old snapshots; no state is set that blocks `apply_diagnosis()`. This is a correctness mismatch between claimed safety behavior and actual control flow.
PROPOSED_FIX: Introduce a real regression lock/defer flag in manager state checked by `apply_diagnosis()`, or downgrade the event text to accurately state that a regression warning was logged without automatic deferral.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F017
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: `false_positive_rate`’s docstring says “last 10 rounds,” but the implementation windows only natural resolutions, not detections. This is a documentation/contract bug that conceals the underlying calibration defect and makes self-diagnosis behavior hard to reason about.
PROPOSED_FIX: Fix the implementation to match the docstring, or revise the docstring to state the true formula. The former is the right fix because the current formula is also behaviorally wrong.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F018
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: The “extended P-pass” implementations (`_extended_p_pass_remediation`, `_p_pass_self_adjustment`) are mostly advisory simulations, not actual iterative falsification with revised candidates rerun under changed assumptions. They loop, but iterations generally inspect the same state and do not isolate an adversarial pass in a fresh context. This means the code claims stronger CDSFL-style P-pass guarantees than it actually provides.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either weaken the claims and rename these routines as heuristic preflight checks, or implement real candidate revision between iterations plus explicit isolated adversarial evaluation state.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F019
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 3
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` documentation says resolved pathologies should shrink windows via decay and persistent ones should widen/grow according to a formal rule, but the inline comments and implementation conflict about directionality (“persistent pathologies don’t reduce window — they escalate severity” vs earlier mathematical comment). This notation/semantic inconsistency obscures intended immune behavior and contributed to the dead `sensitivity_decay` pathway.
PROPOSED_FIX: Rewrite the adaptive-sensitivity comments and formula to match one coherent policy, then implement that policy directly in `effective_window()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F020
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` scans all active remediation state each round and repeatedly pulls full metric histories indirectly; this is acceptable at small scale but grows with experiment length and number of active pathologies. More importantly, because verification is pathology-agnostic, the loop spends work reevaluating remediations that could be checked by a direct predicate tied to the pathology key.
PROPOSED_FIX: Store per-remediation verification callbacks or pathology-specific predicates and evaluate only the minimal needed state. Also expire or consolidate stale remediation records aggressively.
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: the major still-live immune-layer defects are state incompleteness, broken self-calibration metrics, incorrect failure integration, dead per-model anomaly signals, inconsistent remediation verification, and stale/deferred remediation timing. The “no-fix-needed” Exp15 items shown are not challenged by the immune-boundary code provided; the missed issues are chiefly IM_F001, IM_F006, IM_F009, and IM_F016.
